focus: Local staging, tiling, reuse, and load-compute-store. Keep compute off m_axi.
merge_rule: Union of gemm_flatten_v1 and flash_no_RMW overlay. On id conflicts, the no-RMW overlay replaces the v1 entry.

skills.pattern: tiled load/compute/store phase reads x[gi] from m_axi, accumulates into local_x[i], then writes x[gi] back within the same tile iteration — per-tile RMW on external port
skills.strategy: Load the output vector into local memory once (or hold per-element local state across tiles), accumulate entirely in local memory until all contributions for that element are complete, then perform a single store per output element to m_axi.
required_steps: detect per-tile patterns: load x[global_i] → local_x[i] += expr → store x[global_i]
replace with load full or partial x into local_x once before tiled compute, or keep local_x across tile loop without per-tile m_axi writeback
accumulate in local_x[i] or private scalar during compute tiles only
write each m_axi output element once after all tiles that touch that element have finished
if output is too large for one local buffer, tile outputs with local finalize per tile region — still no inner-tile m_axi RMW
guards: extends avoid-no-rmw-m_axi-direct to tiled staging specifically
const m_axi inputs may still be loaded per tile; in-place outputs need local write-back discipline
preserve numerical semantics when deferring store to end of tile sequence
do not apply the blocked transformation when this pattern is present
do not claim success from pragma insertion alone
choose an alternative skill that addresses the actual bottleneck
skills.pattern: perfectly nested loops where Vitis can interchange automatically
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: rewriting the loop nesting order by hand (Vitis 2022.2+ already does this)

skills.pattern: compute loops perform read-modify-write updates directly on arrays mapped to m_axi ports (e.g. A[i][j] = A[i][j] + expr, x[i] = x[i] + expr, w[i] = w[i] + expr inside nested loops)
skills.strategy: Treat every m_axi argument as external DRAM/HBM. Never read and write the same external element inside an inner loop. Do not use global/m_axi arrays as temporary storage or assume HLS will cache m_axi data across iterations.
required_steps: scan every loop for statements that read and write the same m_axi port element
reject direct accumulation into m_axi arrays
reject repeated reads of the same output element from DRAM/HBM inside an inner loop
reject repeated writes to the same output element inside an inner loop
replace with load-compute-store using local buffers or private scalar accumulators
for reductions, accumulate in a private scalar or local array, then write back once
if the full array is too large, tile/block but still finalize each tile locally before one store
guards: preserve numerical semantics when staging into locals
const read-only m_axi inputs may be read once per tile into locals
in-place outputs still require local write-back buffers, not inner-loop RMW on the port
do not include source benchmark names in agent-visible prompts
do not encode baseline-to-target sequences in skill IDs
do not expose private evaluator metadata
skills.pattern: agent attempts to infer or mention the source benchmark suite, hidden test design, target variant sequence, or expected optimization step from skill names or evaluation feedback
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: optimize only from current code, reports, constraints, and feedback; do not assume a benchmark family, stepwise target, or one-shot target

guards: writing an intermediate to global memory only to read it in the immediately following phase is always suspect
this applies even when the intermediate is also an output port
skills.pattern: phase N writes an intermediate array to a global or m_axi output that phase N+1 immediately reads again, even though the value could remain in a local buffer
required_steps: detect producer phase writing global and consumer phase reading the same array
route to hls-chain-intermediate-results-locally
keep the intermediate in local memory until no later phase needs it
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not write intermediates to global memory between dependent phases; route to hls-chain-intermediate-results-locally

guards: accumulators spanning multiple blocks must remain in local memory across block iterations
reloading partial results from global memory inside a block nest wastes bandwidth
skills.pattern: an outer blocking or tiling loop reloads an accumulator or output array from global memory at the start of each block, even though partial results from prior blocks should remain in a local accumulator
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
keep the accumulating buffer in local memory across inner block iterations
load inputs per block if needed, but do not re-fetch the running output from global memory inside the block nest
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: keep the accumulating buffer in local memory across inner block iterations; load inputs per block if needed, but do not re-fetch the running output from global memory inside the block nest

guards: spatial tiling is wrong when each time step must see the full previous field or a full old/new plane
per-tile global store followed by reload in the same iteration wastes bandwidth multiplicatively
prefer ii-raw-dependency-pingpong-old-new-buffers or full-grid local staging when the working set fits
skills.pattern: an outer time-step or iteration loop contains spatial tile loops that load a tile from global memory, compute, store back to global memory, and repeat for every tile before advancing the iteration, instead of keeping the working grid on-chip across the iteration
required_steps: detect whether global load/store happens inside both the iteration loop and the spatial tile loop
estimate total global traffic per iteration; reject if it scales with number of tiles
prefer full-grid local buffers, old/new plane buffers, or line-buffer traversal when legal and on-chip budget allows
route to ii-raw-dependency-pingpong-old-new-buffers or hls-prefer-full-workspace-staging-when-fits
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not use spatial tiling with per-tile global load/store inside each time step or outer iteration; keep the working set on-chip across the iteration using full-grid staging, old/new buffers, or line buffers

guards: complete partition on tile buffers larger than the parallel access width is a red flag
triple-nested tile loops with tiny tiles often increase control overhead without improving reuse
this avoid-rule targets micro-tiling with complete partition of tile buffers — not k-dim banking of a full-workspace GEMM
skills.pattern: nested outer tile loops (for example i0, j0, k0) use a small compile-time tile size with ARRAY_PARTITION complete on multidimensional tile buffers and repeated global reloads per tile
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
prefer hls-prefer-full-workspace-staging-when-fits or larger tiles with cyclic or block partition matched to unroll factor
route to ii-avoid-complete-partition-large-buffer-ff-explosion when complete partition inflates resources
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not use nested small-tile loops with complete partition as default; prefer hls-prefer-full-workspace-staging-when-fits or larger tiles with cyclic or block partition matched to unroll factor

guards: staging only inputs but leaving outputs or accumulators on global memory is incomplete
reading one operand from global inside a pipelined compute loop usually destroys II and bandwidth
skills.pattern: some inputs are loaded into local buffers, but the hot compute loop still reads or writes one or more m_axi array parameters directly, such as an accumulator matrix, temporary, or output array
required_steps: list every array indexed inside each pipelined compute loop
if any index targets a function parameter array, stage that array locally or privatize the accessed region
route to hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate or hls-chain-intermediate-results-locally
validate that compute loops reference only local buffers
skills.strategy: do not mix local staging with global reads or writes in the same hot compute loop; stage all operands and outputs used in compute locally first

guards: avoid-tier skills must not cause fallback to unoptimized reference code
when in doubt, apply hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate rather than emitting textbook C
skills.pattern: the model avoids advanced transforms because of many avoid rules or uncertainty, and responds with textbook nested loops on global arrays and no compute pragmas
required_steps: detect reference-port output despite loaded skill catalog
do not treat caution as permission to skip optimization
apply hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate, hls-multi-phase-local-pipeline, or hls-iterative-stencil-timestep-local-volume as appropriate
ensure PIPELINE pragmas exist before submitting
skills.strategy: avoid rules forbid unsafe transforms, not all transforms; when uncertain, still apply the baseline local load-compute-store recipe instead of reference C

guards: m_axi interface pragmas alone do not constitute optimization
absence of PIPELINE, local buffers, or loop restructuring on a memory-bound hot loop is a blocking defect
skills.pattern: proposed or current code performs the main computation by directly indexing m_axi or global array parameters with no local staging and no HLS pragmas on the hot loops, including multi-phase kernels with many m_axi ports
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate or hls-multi-phase-local-pipeline before any other optimization
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: reject reference-port output even when m_axi interface pragmas are present; route to hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate or hls-multi-phase-local-pipeline before any other optimization

guards: large arrays alone do not justify tiling
local buffering without reuse may add overhead
tiling should change the computation structure or memory traffic pattern
after tiling, check whether compute still uses scalar/global-style access
skills.pattern: a proposed tiling transformation only copies global memory into a local buffer but does not reduce repeated global-memory traffic, improve locality, enable local parallelism, or improve scheduling
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not treat tiling as complete unless the compute is rewritten to use the local tile for reuse or parallelism; otherwise prefer pipelining, coalescing, or dataflow depending on the bottleneck

guards: large arrays alone do not justify tiling
tiling should reduce global-memory traffic, improve locality, resolve II, or enable local parallelism
avoid adding BRAM and copy overhead without measurable benefit
skills.pattern: the loop streams through global memory once with little or no reuse, and tiling would only copy data into a local buffer before immediately using it once
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not apply tiling as the primary optimization; prefer pipelining, coalescing, burst-friendly access, or dataflow unless local staging is required for another transformation

guards: complete partition of a whole large Nd array can destroy timing — prefer partitioning one parallel dim
complete/cyclic on a compile-time k dimension of size ~<=128 for a flattened GEMM is in-scope and often required
do not use resource-heavy partitioning to mask an off-chip bandwidth bottleneck
skills.pattern: a proposed fix completely partitions an entire large local buffer or large multidimensional tile into registers only because there is a memory dependency or port conflict, without targeting the actual parallel access dimension
required_steps: detect whether complete partition is being applied to a large array or large tile
estimate FF/LUT/routing growth from full partitioning
identify the actual parallel access dimension and access count
prefer cyclic/block partitioning, reshape, local banking, or small lane-buffer complete partition
validate whether the alternative resolves II without resource explosion
skills.strategy: do not use complete partition of an entire large buffer as the default; instead partition the parallel access dimension (complete if that dim is modest or required for GEMM flatten; else cyclic/block), or use line buffers / smaller tiles / per-lane small buffers. This avoid-rule does NOT forbid complete/cyclic on GEMM reduction dim k when needed for II=1 flatten.
